answer:
DPO applies softplus to the negative beta-scaled difference between policy and reference preference log ratios. A positive margin means the policy favors the chosen completion more strongly than the reference does. Reference log probabilities are detached. Inputs are sums over valid completion tokens; including prompt/padding tokens or averaging by sequence length changes the objective. Equal ratios produce log(2), which is a useful sanity check.

**Mathematical and practical explanation.** Let $\Delta=\log\pi_\theta(y^+|x)-\log\pi_\theta(y^-|x)-\log\pi_{ref}(y^+|x)+\log\pi_{ref}(y^-|x)$. Then $L=-\log\sigma(\beta\Delta)$. Increasing the chosen-versus-rejected relative margin lowers loss. Completion masking and reference detachment must be correct before interpreting a falling training loss as preference learning. [3](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.18290)

For the implementation or system context discussed above, see [1](https://cameronrwolfe.substack.com/p/direct-preference-optimization) and [2](https://huggingface.co/blog/pref-tuning).
